strengths: Round 7's card was taken almost entirely, and the film is better for it. The Boltzmann machine is planted by voice ('a net that settles as it cools') and paid off correctly in the Nobel citation. Widrow's dream is now specific ('building an artificial brain, for good'), so 'never got over it' lands. 'Buffalo, again: the perceptron's city.' The ch12 reorder puts 'A new door' straight against 'language was the door'. 'Machines had just learned to think longer…' sits on the two shores, where it belongs. OpenAI's founding quote is now attributed to OpenAI, and the Pentagon case ends 'that case, too, is open.'

The spine holds over 33 minutes. The case question (Who taught it?) is answered by one verdict ('Learning, with its accomplices'). One quiet figure runs from 'A tall young man takes his place, far from the flame' to 'Thirty-six years at the edge of the light. Now, it found him.' and on to a 2 a.m. phone call. One device, the candle clock, gives the brief's 'how long people thought that way' a felt duration every time.

The plant-and-payoff web is the best writing in the film, and almost every thread is now closed by ear. 'Put that in the file' is planted three times (the makers' flaw, Rosenblatt's language note, AlexNet's waiting note) and retrieved three times. 'If one exists.' returns as 'No straight cut can separate them.' 'Who paid for dinner?' becomes 'Each man lost one bet.' 'Why choose the fog?' pays off 'Its landscape is one clean bowl'. The student's thesis on rounding errors is paid off, and so is 'practically nothing' from raw text. The lamp in Chicago comes back as 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on'.

The ending is earned and beautiful. 'Never one person. The board was a network all along.' is the film's thesis folded into its own staging. The last line, 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on, and someone at the rim is suspicious. That is where new candles come from.', turns the film's recurring 'At its rim' dissenters into an invitation to the viewer, which is exactly the brief's 'spark curiosity'.

Both deep dives teach real mechanics by ear through inherited, tactile props. AlexNet gets the pierced tin stencil, 'Below zero counts as zero', the weir and the snuffed lanterns. Its noise-to-stencil line is the film's loveliest: 'They began as noise, like television snow. The messenger from 1986 cut them, nudge by nudge.' The two halves that split colour from edges finish on 'Every time.' The transformer gets the question, label and message cards, scored 'the stencil's way'. Then come 'two, nothing, four, two', the jug where 'About half runs to river' (the arithmetic checks out at e² over the sum, about 53%), and the halving explained back from 'Divide by eight'.

The voice is distinct, warm and wry. It saves its one first-person moment for 'You could hear it learn. I love that.' Its dry asides land: 'A winter, then, of prestige, not of use.'; 'Its plan named no rival.'; 'It left out the research, and the chips.'; 'Two signed. The third stood apart.' It is also honest about what is unknown: 'nobody knows exactly when'; 'Still argued.'; 'the accounts differ'; 'Its authors now call that result out of date.'

The emotional low of Act 1 is plain and unforced ('That May, Walter Pitts died alone. McCulloch followed four months later.' / 'on his forty-third birthday, Frank Rosenblatt drowned while sailing.'). It is set up by the film's most likeable line ('“At the moment, none whatever,” Dr. Rosenblatt said cheerfully.'), so the loss is felt rather than reported.

Fairness is part of the drama. The Navy, the press and Rosenblatt all 'fed the hype'. 'Fair credit: that was seven networks voting'. The Swiss lab gets its due, and so does Hinton's 'Google has acted very responsibly'. Three camps are given their own words. China's plan 'named no rival', and Beijing's reply gets its own sentence. Anthropic's FTX money, its book settlement and a contested court case sit under the same light as OpenAI's warning shot.
